children: Overview
U.S. farmland REIT's Q3 net income and adjusted FFO rose sharply yr/yr on higher crop revenues
Results driven by higher participation rents and crop sales, especially pistachios and almonds
Company recorded $2.2 mln non-cash impairment and sold two Florida farms at a net loss
Outlook
Company expects majority of 2026 revenue and earnings to be recognized in second half
Gladstone Land anticipates strong pistachio pricing to partially offset lower 2026 crop yields
Company says almond prices are currently 18%-25% higher than last year
Result Drivers
PARTICIPATION RENTS - Higher participation rents, mainly from early recognition of a bonus payment for the 2025 pistachio crop and strong almond and pistachio prices, drove revenue growth
CROP SALES - Net profit from crop sales on direct-operated farms rose, supported by strong pricing for almonds and pistachios
LEASE MODIFICATIONS - Temporary shift to modified leases with higher participation-based revenues increased reliance on crop results for earnings recognition
